what_it_does: A GPU runs thousands of small programs called kernels simultaneously, but each kernel often stalls while waiting for data to arrive from memory — those idle moments are called warp stalls (a warp is a group of 32 threads that execute together). Running multiple kernels at the same time on the same GPU can hide these stalls by switching to a different kernel's work, but the GPU's default scheduler only interleaves at a coarse level. GoPTX goes much finer: it fuses kernels at the level of PTX (Parallel Thread Execution) instructions — the low-level assembly language that sits just above the hardware on NVIDIA GPUs — by building a merged control-flow graph that interleaves individual instructions from different kernels. A latency-aware weaving algorithm decides which instruction to schedule next so that when one kernel's thread is waiting for data, another kernel's instruction fills the slot, improving the overall rate of useful work per clock cycle.
